revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Practice Room Kits
revealWordProblem.text: The recording studio is setting up 7 identical practice rooms for band camp. Each room needs a music stand ($11) and a tuner ($6). Use the distributive property to find the total cost of stands and tuners for all 7 rooms. Show both the factored form and the expanded form, and explain why they give the same answer.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The total cost is 7(11 + 6). Distributing the 7 to each term: 7 × 11 + 7 × 6 = 77 + 42 = 119. Adding inside the parentheses first gives the same result: 11 + 6 = 17, and 7 × 17 = 119. Both forms equal $119 because the distributive property says 7(11 + 6) = 7 × 11 + 7 × 6.

turnAndTalk.question: Each bundle is a ticket ($15) and a snack ($5). For 3 people, why does 3(15 + 5) give the same $60 as 3 × 15 + 3 × 5?
turnAndTalk.kernel: The distributive property multiplies the 3 by each item, giving the same total.

vocabulary.definition: Multiply a factor by every term inside parentheses.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Multiplicar un factor por cada término dentro de los paréntesis.
vocabulary.cloze: a(b + c) = ab + ___ — the factor reaches ___ term.

vocabulary.definition: Multiplying a number by everything inside the parentheses: a(b + c) = ab + ac.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Multiplicar un número por todo lo que está dentro del paréntesis: a(b + c) = ab + ac.
vocabulary.visual: 3(4 + 5) = 3×4 + 3×5 = 12 + 15 = 27 — the 3 gets 'distributed' to both the 4 and the 5
vocabulary.cloze: The rule that a(b + c) = ab + ac is the ___.

examples.why: The 3 is multiplied by each term inside.

vocabulary.definition: A factor of a whole number divides it evenly, with no remainder. For example, 3 is a factor of 12 because 12 ÷ 3 = 4.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un factor de un número entero lo divide exactamente, sin dejar residuo. Por ejemplo, 3 es un factor de 12 porque 12 ÷ 3 = 4.
vocabulary.visual: In 3(x + 2), the 3 is the factor outside the parentheses that multiplies each term inside
vocabulary.cloze: To rewrite a sum as a product, like 3x + 12 = 3(x + 4), is to ___.

examples.why: It divides with nothing left over.
A factor is never larger than its number.

vocabulary.definition: To multiply out the parentheses in an expression.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Multiplicar lo que está dentro del paréntesis en una expresión.
vocabulary.cloze: To multiply out a product over a sum, like 3(x + 4) = 3x + 12, is to ___.

examples.why: Only the first term was multiplied.

vocabulary.definition: Expressions that always have the same value.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Expresiones que siempre tienen el mismo valor.
vocabulary.visual: 3(x + 4) and 3x + 12 always give the same answer: when x = 2, both = 18; when x = 10, both = 42
vocabulary.cloze: Two expressions that always have the same value are ___.

examples.why: Equal for every value of x.
They differ once x is anything but 1.

vocabulary.definition: The number in front of a letter, like the 3 in 3x.

vocabulary.visual: In 6x + 15, the coefficient of x is 6 — it came from distributing in 3(2x + 5)
vocabulary.cloze: A number multiplied by a variable is a ___.

vocabulary.definition: Terms with the same letter raised to the same power, like 2x and 5x.

conceptIntro.heading: Push further — What is the distributive property?
conceptIntro.intro: You already can do this. So we go up a level, not up a number: find what is always true, show it a second way, and be ready to defend it with a reason instead of an answer.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: The number outside the parentheses gets "shared" with every term inside — and you can say why it is true, and where it would stop being true.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: Each bundle has a ticket ($15) and a snack ($5). For 3 bundles I can write 3(15 + 5).
Way 2: distribute the 3 to each part. 3 × 15 + 3 × 5.
linesEs: Cada paquete tiene un boleto ($15) y un refrigerio ($5). Para 3 paquetes puedo escribir 3(15 + 5).
Manera 2: distribuir el 3 a cada parte. 3 × 15 + 3 × 5.
Las dos maneras dan $60, así que 3(15 + 5) = 3 × 15 + 3 × 5.

weDo.title: Try it together — then prove it
lines: Let's expand 2(8 + 3). Where does the 2 go?
We multiply the 2 by each term: 2 × 8 + 2 × 3.
Now prove it: say why that move had to work at all — not just that it did.
Sentence frame — convince a skeptic: "My method works because ___ . It would stop working if ___ ."
linesEs: Ahora demuéstralo: di por qué ese paso tenía que funcionar — no solo que funcionó.
Marco de oración — convence a alguien que duda: «Mi método funciona porque ___ . Dejaría de funcionar si ___ .»

youDo.title: Now you try — and defend it
lines: Try the problems below on your own. Getting the answer is half the work — be ready to say why your method works, and where it would stop working.
Then pick one problem and show it a second way. If two different methods agree, that agreement is your proof.
linesEs: Intenta los problemas de abajo por tu cuenta. Obtener la respuesta es la mitad del trabajo — prepárate para decir por qué funciona tu método y dónde dejaría de funcionar.
Luego elige un problema y muéstralo de una segunda manera. Si dos métodos distintos coinciden, esa coincidencia es tu prueba.

conceptIntro.headingEs: Ve más allá — ¿Qué es la propiedad distributiva?
conceptIntro.introEs: Esto ya lo sabes hacer. Así que subimos de nivel, no de número: halla lo que siempre es cierto, muéstralo de una segunda manera y prepárate para defenderlo con una razón en lugar de una respuesta.
conceptIntro.keyIdeaEs: El número de afuera del paréntesis se «reparte» con cada término de adentro — y puedes decir por qué es cierto y dónde dejaría de serlo.

explore.instructions: Go deeper: Expand each expression using the distributive property. Then simplify to find the value. As you work, ask yourself WHY it works.

discourse.prompt: What pattern do you see when you expand an expression using the distributive property?
discourse.sentenceFrame: When I distribute, I multiply the outside factor ___ by each term ___. The operation inside the parentheses ___ stays the same.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake
onLevel.correctWork: 5(3x + 2) = 5 × 3x + 5 × 2 = 15x + 10. The student distributed the 5 to the 3x (getting 15x) but left the 2 unchanged. The factor must multiply every term inside, so 5 × 2 = 10, not 2.
hints: The 3x became 15x — what should happen to the 2 when you multiply by 5?
The distributive property says a(b + c) = ab + ac. The 5 must reach both 3x and 2.
onLevel.explanation: The 5 was distributed to the 3x, correctly giving 15x, but the 2 was copied down untouched. Both terms inside must be multiplied: 5(3x + 2) = 5 × 3x + 5 × 2 = 15x + 10, not 15x + 2.
onLevel.explanationEs: El 5 se distribuyó al 3x y dio correctamente 15x, pero el 2 se copió sin cambios. Los dos términos de adentro deben multiplicarse: 5(3x + 2) = 5 × 3x + 5 × 2 = 15x + 10, no 15x + 2.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: 5(3x + 2) = 5 × 3x + 5 × 2 = 15x + 10. El estudiante distribuyó el 5 al 3x (obteniendo 15x) pero dejó el 2 sin cambiar. El factor debe multiplicar cada término de adentro, así que 5 × 2 = 10, no 2.
hintsEs: El 3x se convirtió en 15x — ¿qué debe pasar con el 2 al multiplicar por 5?
La propiedad distributiva dice a(b + c) = ab + ac. El 5 debe llegar tanto a 3x como al 2.

onLevel.title: Find the Distributive Error
onLevel.correctWork: 5(2x + 4) = 5 × 2x + 5 × 4 = 10x + 20. You must distribute the 5 to BOTH terms inside the parentheses, not just the first one.
hints: Did the student multiply 5 by both terms, or only the first term?
The distributive property says a(b + c) = ab + ac. Both b and c get multiplied.
onLevel.titleEs: Encuentra el error de la propiedad distributiva
onLevel.explanation: The 5 multiplied only the first term inside. Distributing to both gives 5(2x + 4) = 5 × 2x + 5 × 4 = 10x + 20. Testing with x = 1 confirms it: the original 5(2 + 4) = 30 and 10(1) + 20 = 30, while the student's 10x + 4 would give only 14.
onLevel.explanationEs: El 5 multiplicó solo el primer término de adentro. Al distribuir a los dos: 5(2x + 4) = 5 × 2x + 5 × 4 = 10x + 20. Probar con x = 1 lo confirma: la expresión original 5(2 + 4) = 30 y 10(1) + 20 = 30, mientras que el 10x + 4 del estudiante daría apenas 14.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: 5(2x + 4) = 5 × 2x + 5 × 4 = 10x + 20. Debes distribuir el 5 a AMBOS términos dentro del paréntesis, no solo al primero.
hintsEs: ¿El estudiante multiplicó el 5 por los dos términos, o solo por el primero?
La propiedad distributiva dice a(b + c) = ab + ac. Se multiplican tanto b como c.

onLevel.prompt: Use the distributive property to explain why 6 × 98 can be calculated as 6 × 100 − 6 × 2 = 588. Then create your own example of using the distributive property to make multiplication easier.
onLevel.hint: Use the Distributive Property to expand, showing how each term is multiplied by the factor outside.
hints: 98 is awkward, but it's close to a friendly number: 98 = 100 − 2.
Rewrite 6 × 98 as 6(100 − 2), then distribute the 6 to both the 100 and the 2.
Compute the easy products 6 × 100 and 6 × 2, subtract, then build your own example the same way.
onLevel.explanation: Because 98 = 100 − 2, you can rewrite 6 × 98 as 6(100 − 2) and distribute: 6 × 100 − 6 × 2 = 600 − 12 = 588. The distributive property is what makes that rewrite legal, and it turns one hard multiplication into two easy ones — the same trick works for problems like 7 × 99 or 4 × 52.
onLevel.explanationEs: Como 98 = 100 − 2, puedes reescribir 6 × 98 como 6(100 − 2) y distribuir: 6 × 100 − 6 × 2 = 600 − 12 = 588. La propiedad distributiva es lo que permite ese cambio, y convierte una multiplicación difícil en dos fáciles; el mismo truco sirve para problemas como 7 × 99 o 4 × 52.
onLevel.promptEs: Usa la propiedad distributiva para explicar por qué 6 × 98 se puede calcular como 6 × 100 − 6 × 2 = 588. Después crea tu propio ejemplo de cómo usar la propiedad distributiva para hacer más fácil una multiplicación.
hintsEs: 98 es incómodo, pero está cerca de un número amigable: 98 = 100 − 2.
Reescribe 6 × 98 como 6(100 − 2) y luego distribuye el 6 tanto al 100 como al 2.
Calcula los productos fáciles 6 × 100 y 6 × 2, resta, y luego arma tu propio ejemplo del mismo modo.

onLevel.stem: Light Cue 1: Expand 3(x + 4) for the stage-light controller.
onLevel.explanation: Distribute the 3 to each term: 3 × x + 3 × 4 = 3x + 12.
choiceFeedback: The 3 was multiplied by x but not by the 4. Every term inside the parentheses gets multiplied.
You added 3 + 4 first, but you need to multiply 3 by each term.
It looks like 3 and 4 were added instead of multiplied. Distributing is a multiplication move, not an addition one.
onLevel.stemEs: Señal de luz 1: desarrolla 3(x + 4) para el controlador de luces del escenario.
onLevel.explanationEs: Distribuye el 3 a cada término: 3 × x + 3 × 4 = 3x + 12.
hints: The distributive property says a(b + c) = ab + ac — the outside factor multiplies every term inside.
Write it as two separate multiplications: 3 times x, and 3 times 4.
3 × x gives 3x. Now find 3 × 4 and write the two products with the + sign between them.
hintsEs: La propiedad distributiva dice que a(b + c) = ab + ac: el factor de afuera multiplica cada término de adentro.
Escríbelo como dos multiplicaciones separadas: 3 por x y 3 por 4.
3 × x da 3x. Ahora halla 3 × 4 y escribe los dos productos con el signo + entre ellos.

extending.instructions: Use the distributive property to expand each expression.
hints: Some inside terms have coefficients, like 2x. Multiply the outside number by the WHOLE term: 3 × 2x.
Two products per row: outside × first term, outside × second term. Keep the − sign if the inside subtracts.
Row 1: 3(2x + 5) → 3 × 2x = 6x. Now multiply 3 × 5 and join the products with +. Repeat for each row.
extending.explanation: The outside factor multiplies the whole term inside, coefficient included, and the sign inside stays the same. So 3(2x + 5) = 6x + 15, 7(a − 4) = 7a − 28, 2(3m + 8) = 6m + 16, and 5(6 − y) = 30 − 5y.
extending.explanationEs: El factor de afuera multiplica el término completo de adentro, incluido su coeficiente, y el signo de adentro se mantiene igual. Así, 3(2x + 5) = 6x + 15, 7(a − 4) = 7a − 28, 2(3m + 8) = 6m + 16 y 5(6 − y) = 30 − 5y.
extending.instructionsEs: Usa la propiedad distributiva para desarrollar cada expresión.
hintsEs: Algunos términos de adentro tienen coeficiente, como 2x. Multiplica el número de afuera por el término COMPLETO: 3 × 2x.
Dos productos por fila: afuera × primer término y afuera × segundo término. Conserva el signo − si adentro hay resta.
Fila 1: 3(2x + 5) → 3 × 2x = 6x. Ahora multiplica 3 × 5 y une los productos con +. Repite en cada fila.

extending.label: Match each factored form to its expanded form.
hints: Each factored card expands into exactly one card on the other side. Distribute before you match.
Expand on scrap paper: multiply the outside number by both inside terms, watching + versus − signs.
Start with 2(x + 9): find 2 × x and 2 × 9, then look for the card showing that sum.
extending.explanation: Distributing each factored card produces exactly one expanded card: 2(x + 9) = 2x + 18, 5(3n − 2) = 15n − 10, 4(a + 6) = 4a + 24, 3(7 − y) = 21 − 3y, 6(2m + 1) = 12m + 6, and 8(x − 3) = 8x − 24. Watch the signs — subtraction inside stays subtraction after you expand.
extending.explanationEs: Al distribuir, cada tarjeta factorizada produce exactamente una tarjeta expandida: 2(x + 9) = 2x + 18, 5(3n − 2) = 15n − 10, 4(a + 6) = 4a + 24, 3(7 − y) = 21 − 3y, 6(2m + 1) = 12m + 6 y 8(x − 3) = 8x − 24. Cuida los signos: la resta de adentro sigue siendo resta después de expandir.
extending.labelEs: Une cada forma factorizada con su forma desarrollada.
hintsEs: Cada tarjeta factorizada se desarrolla en exactamente una tarjeta del otro lado. Distribuye antes de unir.
Desarrolla en papel: multiplica el número de afuera por ambos términos de adentro, cuidando los signos + y −.
Empieza con 2(x + 9): halla 2 × x y 2 × 9, y luego busca la tarjeta que muestre esa suma.

extending.stem: Light Cue 2: Expand 5(2 + n) to set two spotlight banks.
extending.explanation: Distribute the 5 to each term: 5 × 2 + 5 × n = 10 + 5n.
choiceFeedback: The 5 reached the 2 but not the n. Both terms inside the parentheses need that factor.
Multiply 5 by each term inside: 5 × 2 = 10, and 5 × n = 5n.
You need to distribute the 5 to both the 2 and the n.
extending.stemEs: Señal de luz 2: desarrolla 5(2 + n) para ajustar dos bancos de reflectores.
extending.explanationEs: Distribuye el 5 a cada término: 5 × 2 + 5 × n = 10 + 5n.
hints: The factor outside multiplies both terms, whether the number or the variable comes first.
Break it into 5 times 2 and 5 times n, then write the two products in the same order.
5 × 2 = 10. Now find 5 × n and join the two results with the + sign.
hintsEs: El factor de afuera multiplica los dos términos, sin importar si primero va el número o la variable.
Sepáralo en 5 por 2 y 5 por n, y luego escribe los dos productos en el mismo orden.
5 × 2 = 10. Ahora halla 5 × n y une los dos resultados con el signo +.

extending.stem: Light Cue 3: Expand 4(a + 2) for the back-row beam.
extending.explanation: Distribute the 4 to each term: 4 × a + 4 × 2 = 4a + 8.
choiceFeedback: The 4 multiplied the a, but the 2 was copied down unchanged. The second term needs multiplying too.
The 4 reached the 2 but skipped the a. The variable term needs that factor just as much.
Don't multiply 4 + 2 first. Distribute 4 to both terms.
extending.stemEs: Señal de luz 3: desarrolla 4(a + 2) para el haz de la última fila.
extending.explanationEs: Distribuye el 4 a cada término: 4 × a + 4 × 2 = 4a + 8.
hints: Distributing hands the outside factor to every term inside the parentheses.
Set up two products: 4 times a, and 4 times 2.
4 × a gives 4a. Now compute 4 × 2 and write the sum of the two products.
hintsEs: Distribuir entrega el factor de afuera a cada término dentro del paréntesis.
Plantea dos productos: 4 por a y 4 por 2.
4 × a da 4a. Ahora calcula 4 × 2 y escribe la suma de los dos productos.

extending.title: Level 2 Extension — The Spotlight Only Hit One Term
extending.correctWork: 3(x + 4) = 3 × x + 3 × 4 = 3x + 12. The factor 3 is like a spotlight that must shine on EVERY term inside the parentheses, not just the first one. Picture the area model: a 3-by-x panel (3x) plus a 3-by-4 panel (12).
hints: Did the 3 reach both terms inside the parentheses, or only the x?
The distributive property says a(b + c) = ab + ac — both b and c get multiplied.
extending.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2: El reflector solo alumbró un término
extending.explanation: The 3 shone on the x but skipped the 4. Distributing to every term gives 3(x + 4) = 3 × x + 3 × 4 = 3x + 12. An area model shows why: a 3-by-x panel is 3x and a 3-by-4 panel is 12, and the whole rectangle is both panels together.
extending.explanationEs: El 3 alumbró la x pero se saltó el 4. Al distribuir a cada término: 3(x + 4) = 3 × x + 3 × 4 = 3x + 12. Un modelo de área lo muestra: un panel de 3 por x es 3x y un panel de 3 por 4 es 12, y el rectángulo completo son los dos paneles juntos.
extending.correctWorkEs: 3(x + 4) = 3 × x + 3 × 4 = 3x + 12. El factor 3 es como un reflector que debe iluminar CADA término dentro del paréntesis, no solo el primero. Imagina el modelo de área: un panel de 3-por-x (3x) más un panel de 3-por-4 (12).
hintsEs: ¿El 3 llegó a los dos términos dentro del paréntesis, o solo a la x?
La propiedad distributiva dice a(b + c) = ab + ac — se multiplican tanto b como c.

choiceFeedback: The 6 was multiplied by n but the 3 was copied down unchanged. The factor outside has to reach every term inside the parentheses.
Did you only multiply 6 by n? You also need 6 × 3 = 18.
Distribute 6 to both terms inside the parentheses.
hints: The 6 outside must visit BOTH terms inside the parentheses: the n and the 3.
Multiply 6 × n and 6 × 3 separately, then join the two products with the plus sign.
First product: 6 × n = 6n. Now find the second product 6 × 3 and add it on.
hintsEs: El 6 de afuera debe visitar AMBOS términos dentro del paréntesis: la n y el 3.
Multiplica 6 × n y 6 × 3 por separado y luego une los dos productos con el signo más.
Primer producto: 6 × n = 6n. Ahora halla el segundo producto 6 × 3 y súmalo.

extending.explanation: The GCF of 12 and 18 is 6: 12x + 18 = 6(2x + 3). Check by expanding: 6 × 2x = 12x and 6 × 3 = 18.
extending.explanationEs: El MCD de 12 y 18 es 6: 12x + 18 = 6(2x + 3). Comprueba desarrollando: 6 × 2x = 12x y 6 × 3 = 18.
choiceFeedback: Expand it — 2(6x + 9) does equal 12x + 18, but 6x and 9 still share a factor. Factoring with the GCF leaves nothing else to pull out.
Expand to check: 12 × 18 = 216, not 18. Only the 12x term was considered.
Expand to check: 6 × 18 = 108, not 18. The second term inside must multiply back to 18.
choiceFeedbackEs: Desarróllala: 2(6x + 9) sí es igual a 12x + 18, pero 6x y 9 todavía comparten un factor. Factorizar con el MCD no deja nada más por sacar.
Comprueba desarrollando: 12 × 18 = 216, no 18. Solo se consideró el término 12x.
Comprueba desarrollando: 6 × 18 = 108, no 18. El término de adentro debe multiplicar de vuelta a 18.
hints: Factoring runs the distributive property backwards: what number divides BOTH 12 and 18?
The greatest common factor of 12 and 18 is 6. Divide each term by it.
12x ÷ 6 = 2x and 18 ÷ 6 = 3. Write the factored form, then expand it to check.
hintsEs: Factorizar es la propiedad distributiva al revés: ¿qué número divide a 12 Y a 18?
El máximo común divisor de 12 y 18 es 6. Divide cada término entre él.
12x ÷ 6 = 2x y 18 ÷ 6 = 3. Escribe la forma factorizada y desarróllala para comprobar.

extending.stemEs: Factoriza 24a + 16 por completo, usando el MCD.
extending.explanation: The GCF of 24 and 16 is 8: 24a + 16 = 8(3a + 2). Expanding gives 24a + 16 back, and 3a and 2 share no factor.
extending.explanationEs: El MCD de 24 y 16 es 8: 24a + 16 = 8(3a + 2). Al desarrollar regresa 24a + 16, y 3a y 2 no comparten factores.
choiceFeedback: 4(6a + 4) expands to 24a + 16, but 6a and 4 still share a 2 — the factoring is not complete. What is the GREATEST common factor?
Expand: 8 × 8 = 64, not 16. Check the second term inside the parentheses.
Expand: 16 × a = 16a, not 24a. The first term no longer matches.
choiceFeedbackEs: 4(6a + 4) se desarrolla a 24a + 16, pero 6a y 4 todavía comparten un 2 — la factorización no está completa. ¿Cuál es el MÁXIMO factor común?
Desarrolla: 8 × 8 = 64, no 16. Revisa el segundo término de adentro.
Desarrolla: 16 × a = 16a, no 24a. El primer término ya no coincide.
hints: List the factors 24 and 16 share; take the greatest.
The GCF is 8. Divide both terms by 8.
24a ÷ 8 = 3a and 16 ÷ 8 = 2. Write it, then expand to confirm nothing is lost.
hintsEs: Enumera los factores que comparten 24 y 16; toma el mayor.
El MCD es 8. Divide ambos términos entre 8.
24a ÷ 8 = 3a y 16 ÷ 8 = 2. Escríbelo y desarrolla para confirmar que nada se pierde.

extending.stem: Which expression is NOT equivalent to 6x + 12?
extending.explanation: 6(x + 12) expands to 6x + 72 — the 12 was left unmultiplied. The other three all expand to exactly 6x + 12.
extending.explanationEs: 6(x + 12) se desarrolla a 6x + 72: el 12 quedó sin multiplicar por completo. Las otras tres sí dan exactamente 6x + 12.
choiceFeedback: Expand it: 6 × x = 6x and 6 × 2 = 12. This one IS equivalent — you need the impostor.
Expand it: 2 × 3x = 6x and 2 × 6 = 12. Equivalent — keep hunting.
Expand it: 3 × 2x = 6x and 3 × 4 = 12. Equivalent — one of the others fails the check.
choiceFeedbackEs: Desarróllala: 6 × x = 6x y 6 × 2 = 12. Esta SÍ es equivalente — busca la impostora.
Desarróllala: 3 × 2x = 6x y 3 × 4 = 12. Equivalente — otra opción falla la comprobación.
hints: Expand each choice and compare it with 6x + 12.
A factored form is equivalent only if BOTH products land back on the original terms.
Check the constant each expansion produces: 6 × 12, 6 × 2, 2 × 6, 3 × 4. Which is not 12?
hintsEs: Desarrolla cada opción y compárala con 6x + 12.
Una forma factorizada es equivalente solo si AMBOS productos regresan a los términos originales.
Revisa la constante de cada desarrollo: 6 × 12, 6 × 2, 2 × 6, 3 × 4. ¿Cuál no es 12?

extending.correctWork: The correct answer is 6(2x + 3). The GCF of 12 and 18 is 6: 12x + 18 = 6(2x + 3). Check by expanding: 6 × 2x = 12x and 6 × 3 = 18.
extending.correctWorkEs: La respuesta correcta es 6(2x + 3). El MCD de 12 y 18 es 6: 12x + 18 = 6(2x + 3). Comprueba desarrollando: 6 × 2x = 12x y 6 × 3 = 18.
hints: Factoring runs the distributive property backwards: what number divides BOTH 12 and 18?
hintsEs: Factorizar es la propiedad distributiva al revés: ¿qué número divide a 12 Y a 18?

practice.commonMistake: The most common mistake in The Distributive Property is multiplying the outside factor by only the FIRST term inside the parentheses and forgetting the second — for example, writing 3(x + 4) = 3x + 4 instead of 3x + 12. Before you submit, check: did the outside number reach BOTH terms inside the parentheses?

optionalActivity.name: Distributive Property Stage Lights
optionalActivity.intro: Challenge — prove it: Program the studio's stage lights by distributing each factor to every term in the cue. Convince a skeptic your answer is right.

diagram.title: Distributing 8(12 + 9)
diagram.caption: Each row is one product from distributing the 8 — stands (8×$12=$96) and stools (8×$9=$72) — and together they fill the $168 total, showing 8(12+9)=8×12+8×9.

connect.scenario: A music studio is ordering supplies for 8 practice rooms. Each room needs a music stand ($12) and a stool ($9). The total cost can be written as 8(12 + 9).
connect.promptQuestion: Use the distributive property to find the total cost. Which way of calculating is easier for you?
connect.prompt: 8(12 + 9) = 8 × ___ + 8 × ___ = ___ + ___ = ___. I think the ___ form is easier because ___.

check.explanation: The distributive property multiplies the 8 by EACH term inside the parentheses.

check.stem: What is the total cost for 8 practice rooms?
check.explanation: 8 × 12 + 8 × 9 = 96 + 72 = $168. Adding inside first gives the same answer: 8 × 21 = $168.

check.stem: A student wrote 8(12 + 9) = 8 × 12 + 9 = 105. What went wrong?
choices: They forgot to multiply the 9 by 8 as well
check.explanation: Distributing means the 8 multiplies BOTH terms: 8 × 12 AND 8 × 9. Skipping the second one loses $63.

connect.modelAnswer: 8(12 + 9) = 8 × 12 + 8 × 9 = 96 + 72 = $168. You can also add inside the parentheses first: 8 × 21 = $168. Both routes give the same total — that is exactly what the distributive property guarantees.

exitTicket.stem: Explain your thinking — Which expression is equivalent to 7(x + 3)?
exitTicket.explanation: 7(x + 3) = 7 × x + 7 × 3 = 7x + 21. The 7 must multiply BOTH terms — multiplying only the x gives 7x + 3, multiplying only the 3 gives x + 21, and adding 7 + 3 instead of multiplying gives 7x + 10.
choiceFeedback: The 7 reached the x but skipped the 3. Distributing multiplies EVERY term inside — what is 7 × 3?
The 7 reached the 3 but skipped the x. Both terms inside the parentheses get multiplied by 7.
The 10 comes from ADDING 7 + 3. Distributing multiplies across, so the constant term should be 7 × 3.
hints: The 7 outside has to multiply BOTH terms inside — the x and the 3.
Form two products and join them with +. Multiplying only one of the terms is the classic trap.
First product: 7 × x = 7x. Now multiply 7 × 3 and attach that product with a plus sign before choosing.

questions.stem: In the prime factorization of 50, how many times does 5 appear?
questions.stemEs: En la descomposición en factores primos de 50, ¿cuántas veces aparece el 5?
questions.explanationEs: 50 = 2 × 25 = 2 × 5 × 5, así que el 5 aparece dos veces.
